title: Complexity Dependent Error Rates for Physics-informed Statistical Learning via the Small-ball Method
abstract: arXiv:2510.23149v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Physics-informed statistical learning (PISL) integrates empirical data with physical knowledge to enhance the statistical performance of estimators. While PISL methods are widely used in practice, a comprehensive theoretical understanding of how informed regularization affects statistical properties is still missing. Specifically, two fundamental questions have yet to be fully addressed: (A) what is the trade-off between soft penalties and hard constraints, and (B) what is the statistical gain of incorporating physical knowledge compared to purely data-driven empirical error minimisation. In this paper, we address these questions for PISL in classes of functions whose convex hull satisfies a small-ball condition, in particular convex classes, under physical knowledge expressed as linear equations by developing appropriate complexity dependent error rates based on the small-ball method. translated_title: 基于小球方法的物理信息统计学习的复杂度相关误差率
translated_abstract: 物理信息统计学习将经验数据与物理知识相结合，以提升估计器的统计性能。尽管PISL方法在实践中被广泛使用，但目前仍缺乏对信息正则化如何影响统计性质的全面理论理解。具体而言，两个基本问题尚未得到充分解答：（A）软惩罚与硬约束之间的权衡是什么，（B）与纯数据驱动的经验误差最小化相比，引入物理知识能带来多大的统计增益。本文针对凸包满足小球条件的函数类（尤其是凸函数类），在以线性方程形式表达的物理知识下，通过基于小球方法构建适当的复杂度相关误差率，来解答上述两个问题。我们进一步将这些结论具体化到有限维d的线性函数类（摘要在此处截断）。
tldr: 本文通过小球方法为物理信息统计学习建立了复杂度相关的误差率，回答了软惩罚与硬约束之间的权衡问题，并量化了引入物理知识相较于纯数据驱动方法所带来的统计增益。
en_tdlr: This paper develops complexity-dependent error rates for physics-informed statistical learning via the small-ball method, addressing the trade-off between soft penalties and hard constraints and quantifying the statistical gain of incorporating physical knowledge over purely data-driven empirical risk minimization.
